corpus.title: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
corpus.signal_text:
Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
- Published
A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko has said, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.
The attack on Saturday morning injured two people, and damaged the road surface and overhead trolleybus wires on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, Klitschko said, causing traffic jams.
It comes after the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times by Russian drones this week, with Klitschko warning that "the enemy is tearing Kyiv apart".
Russia said its drones had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops and military cargo. Moscow again urged foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv.
The two Kyiv bridges across the Dnipro River link the western and eastern parts of the capital and had not been hit before Thursday, signalling a news stage in Moscow's strategy.
Attacks on the Pivdennyi Bridge had earlier caused major travel disruption, with metro and car travel across it suspended.
Many of the city's residents - which number about three million - rely on the metro to travel across the city every day.
Writing on Telegram on Saturday morning, Klitschko said "emergency services are on their way" after the Pivnichnyi Bridge was hit.
"Traffic on the bridge from the left to the right bank is currently blocked," he added.
Earlier attacks on the Pivdennyi Bridge prompted Kyiv's defence council to hold a crisis meeting on Friday.
Klitschko warned afterwards that the city was now in a "very dramatic situation" as Moscow was battering its "critical infrastructure, logistics, housing" and other key facilities.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Russia is acting in response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities, despite the fact that it was Moscow that had first launched such attacks.
After the Pivdennyi Bridge was attacked, passengers described how dust from a blast wave entered their carriage through the ventilation system.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Putin had decided that there were "no rules now" when attacking Ukraine.
In an interview with the Financial Times, he said: "The Russians have failed to occupy us. So now they are carrying out massive attacks and mass killings."
He added: "They want to destroy our bridges... our data centres, the internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to flee their cities."

corpus.title: Russian forces strike a second major Kyiv bridge across the Dnipro after two days of attacks on the South Bridge
corpus.signal_text:
Russian forces strike a second major Kyiv bridge across the Dnipro after two days of attacks on the South Bridge
Russian forces struck Kyiv’s Northern Bridge on the morning of October 3, damaging the road surface and overhead trolleybus power lines. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the bridge was partially closed to traffic.
On October 1 and 2, Russia carried out at least three drone attacks on Kyiv’s Southern Bridge, damaging a support, a guardrail, the road surface, and the metro’s protective concrete barrier. The bridge was closed to all traffic.
BBC Ukrainian reported that these were the first strikes of the war on Kyiv’s bridges across the Dnipro River.
Kyiv has nine bridges across the Dnipro, carrying road, pedestrian, and rail traffic. The Northern and Southern bridges are among the busiest and most important river crossings. In the preceding days, strikes on the two bridges also prompted partial traffic closures on other Kyiv bridges. Traffic jams formed in the city.

corpus.title: Russia hits major Kyiv bridge, logistics hub in latest attack
corpus.signal_text:
Russia struck a key bridge in Kyiv connecting the left and right bank of the Dnipro river overnight Saturday, as Moscow steps up its aerial campaign against Ukraine.
Traffic was suspended on the capital’s Northern Bridge and emergency services were deployed to the scene amid damage to the road and trolleybus cables on the crossing, Kyiv major Vitaly Klitschko said on Saturday. Around 500,000 people commute from the Dnipro’s left bank to the river’s right bank daily, with eight bridges connecting the two sides in total.
That follows several similar attacks by drones on the Southern Bridge in Kyiv in recent days, forcing the temporary suspension of vehicle movement and huge traffic jams.

Ukraine-Russia war latest: Second major bridge in Kyiv comes under Russian air attack
Northern Bridge across Dnipro river target of new Russian air attack, mayor Vitali Klitschko says

The Northern Bridge across the Dnipro river in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv was hit during a Russian air attack on Saturday, mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
Emergency services were deployed to the scene and traffic across the bridge from the east to the west bank was suspended following damage to the road surface and the overhead trolleybus cables.
There were no casualties reported. In the past two days, the Southern Bridge has been struck several times by Russian drones, forcing the temporary suspension of traffic across it and two other bridges across the river.
Earlier, Lithuania’s Vilnius airport was closed for an hour and Nato jets were scrambled after a suspected drone was reported to be flying into the country from Belarus, the country's National Crisis Management Centre said.
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has said his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, has instructed his generals to abandon the rules of war to capture more territory in Ukraine.
Russia has increasingly targeted Ukrainian cities, hitting key infrastructure that is keeping Ukraine’s war-battered economy afloat. Recent targets have included key industries, railways, data centres, energy infrastructure, as well as schools and hospitals.
Zelensky says Putin has told his generals 'there are no rules now' in Ukraine war
Volodymyr Zelensky says Russian president Vladimir Putin has instructed his generals to abandon the rules of war in pursuit of more territory in Ukraine, according to the Financial Times.
The Ukrainian president made the remarks during a visit to a bomb shelter inside a school that had been hit by a Russian drone on Thursday.
Zelensky said Putin gave the order last month, saying: "He said there are no rules now." Russia has since stepped up its air strikes on civilian targets, particularly in Kyiv, hitting data centres and energy infrastructure as well as schools and hospitals.
Russia still formally denies that it strikes civilian targets, and typically justifies its strikes as hitting military-linked buildings or infrastructure.

corpus.signal_text:
Two injured in Russian strike on Northern Bridge in Kyiv
Ukrinform
Two people were injured in a Russian strike on the Northern Bridge in Kyiv on Saturday.
According to Ukrinform, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said this in a Telegram post.
"Two people were injured this morning as a result of the enemy strike on the Northern Bridge in the capital. Medics provided medical assistance to one of the injured at the scene. The second person was hospitalized and is now receiving outpatient treatment," the mayor said.
As reported, the roadway and trolleybus overhead contact network on Kyiv's Northern Bridge were damaged in a Russian attack early on October 3. Traffic remained restricted, with three lanes operating from the left bank to the right bank of the Dnipro River, and one lane from the right bank to the left.
